title: Bot trading with AI
author: kishorekkota
selftext: I am working on building a bot leveraging alpaca market data and IB Pro api. Still building strategy that works based on last 3 months historical data using Claude and Codex. Wanted to check if anyone tried and any tips.

comments.author: Remarkable-Duty8067
comments.body: Expand Datapool, 2015 - today should do it. Kill survivorship biased ticker, find a method to take look ahead bias into account, markout a holdout zone (1-2 last years), dont forget commissions, fees, slippage. Harden your fixed parameters by multiple testruns.

replies.author: frank_stasi
replies.body: Did you find a configuration that actually worked?

comments.author: frank_stasi
comments.body:
I’m building something similar, focused on day trading only.

Experimented with a bunch of fixed strategies using various signals.   
Nothing really worked, not even on backtesting (because I know how to do things and I never over fit): I gave the algo 5k and it basically earned 60bucks a month. Definitely too low.

Now I’m trying a different strategy and building an actual ML model (XGBoost) instead of an algorithm.  
The pipeline / datascience part works extremely well but it’s genuinely hard to find causal features that perform well enough.

I’m a grizzled software engineer with some data science expertise, but I lack deep financial knowledge, if someone wants to join forces feel free to DM me.

replies.author: Weird_Cookie1700
replies.body:
I built a game that will do the day trading. Uses real time data, the AI will make the trades in game, you just follow them in real life.

It’ll also predict 15 stocks (ish) that it thinks are going up at least 1% for the day and it’s 84% accurate over back data and real historical since March 2026. They’re predicted at 915am EST everyday so I kinda use them to walk into the day with equity.

I have another engine that tells me a simple yes or no on whether a stock will go up within 30 minutes and what kind of return I can expect. I let that run all day.

The intraday engine that buys stocks uses a stop loss of -.9 and activates a trail at .2 that has a reversal of -.9 also, i find that’s the best for the stocks I trade.

I’m trying to figure out a way to teach it that logic to read graphs but that’s a lost cause I think.
